To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

preoperative computed tomography (CT) assessment of skeletal muscle index (SMI) is a valuable predictor of perioperative outcomes in patients undergoing major hepatectomy (MH) for perihilar biliary cancer.

the preoperative CT evaluation of skeletal muscle mass in patients undergoing hepatectomy is a useful predictor of postoperative complications, and the preoperative CT assessment of the liver is an independent predictor of the postoperative liver failure.

preoperative CT assessment of skeletal muscle area (SMA) is a valuable predictor of postoperative complications and mortality in patients undergoing hepatectomy with or without vascular reconstruction for perihilar biliary cancer, and that SMA may be a better predictor of postoperative outcomes than the preoperative nutritional markers albumin and body mass index.
